messages.author: e8ad54d4ad5b752c
messages.subject: One ggplot2 question
parts:
Thanks for the assistance on previous questions, I figured out most of
them before getting responses. I have one last lingering issue.

I am trying to reduce the white/open space between the graph/barplot
itself and the axis labels. It seems like there is a lot of space
between.

messages.author: e8ad54d4ad5b752c
messages.subject: Re: One ggplot2 question
parts:
A picture and code to go with.

g <- ggplot(AGGDATA, aes(x=year, y=freq, fill=PROD))
g <- g + geom_bar(stat="identity", binwidth=1, width=.65) + theme_bw()
g <- g + theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor=
element_blank(), panel.border=element_blank(),
panel.margin=unit(-1,"mm"))
g <- g + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=5, vjust=0), plot.title=
element_text(size=14, face="bold"), axis.title.x=element_text
(face="bold", vjust=2, size=10), axis.title.y=element_text(face="bold",
vjust=1, size=10), axis.ticks.margin=unit(1, "cm"))
g <- g + theme(legend.justification=c(0,1), legend.position=c(.05,.97),
axis.ticks=element_blank(), axis.text.y=element_text(hjust=1.8,
vjust=0))
g <- g + scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1988,2013,1), labels=yrs, expand=c(0,0))
g <- g + scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 6000,500), expand=c(0,0))
g

messages.author: 26bf2c8b537713d9
messages.subject: Re: One ggplot2 question
parts:
Hi Rachel,

Two thoughts:
You might try messing with theme(axis.ticks.margin = unit(n, "unitname")), where n is numeric and unitname is one of the ones listed at https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/grid/html/unit.html.

If that's not good enough, you may wish to consider producing a larger output image. Line widths, margins, and a bunch of other things in ggplot2 are defined in terms of "real" units, so they'll take up a smaller percentage of a bigger plot.

Hope this helps!
Peter
